title: Pair With Target Sum
description:
You are given a list of distinct integers and a target value. Exactly one pair of positions i < j has values that add up to the target. Find that pair.

Input format:
Line 1: two integers n and target.
Line 2: n distinct integers.

Output format:
Two integers i and j (0-based, i < j), separated by a space.

Constraints:
2 <= n <= 100000, values fit in a 32-bit signed integer, exactly one valid pair exists.

visibleTestCases.explanation: Positions 0 and 1 hold 2 and 7, which add up to 9.
Positions 1 and 2 hold 2 and 4, which add up to 6.

title: Best Contiguous Stretch
description:
Given a list of integers (positive, zero or negative), find the largest possible sum of a non-empty contiguous block of the list.

Input format:
Line 1: integer n.
Line 2: n integers.

Output format:
One integer, the largest block sum.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 100000, |value| <= 10000.

visibleTestCases.explanation: The block 4, -1, 2, 1 sums to 6, and no block does better.
Every number is negative, so the best block is the single value -1.

title: Ways To Climb
description:
A staircase has n steps. You can climb either 1 or 2 steps at a time. Count the number of different ways to reach the top.

Input format:
One integer n.

Output format:
One integer, the number of distinct ways.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 45.

visibleTestCases.explanation: The ways are 1+1+1, 1+2 and 2+1, so the answer is 3.
The ways are 1+1+1+1, 1+1+2, 1+2+1, 2+1+1 and 2+2, so the answer is 5.

title: Fewest Coins
description:
You have an unlimited supply of coins of the given denominations. Find the smallest number of coins needed to make exactly the target amount, or report -1 if it cannot be done.

Input format:
Line 1: two integers n (number of denominations) and amount.
Line 2: n distinct positive integers, the denominations.

Output format:
One integer, the minimum number of coins, or -1.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 12, 1 <= amount <= 10000, each denomination <= 10000.

visibleTestCases.explanation: Use 5 + 5 + 1, which is three coins.
Coins of value 2 can never add up to 3, so the answer is -1.

title: Count The Islands
description:
A map is a grid of 0s (water) and 1s (land). Land cells that touch each other horizontally or vertically belong to the same island. Count the islands.

Input format:
Line 1: two integers r and c.
Next r lines: a string of c characters, each 0 or 1 (no spaces).

Output format:
One integer, the number of islands.

Constraints:
1 <= r, c <= 300.

visibleTestCases.explanation: There are three islands: the 2x2 block, the single cell in the middle, and the pair at the bottom right.
The corners only touch the centre diagonally, so each of the five land cells is its own island.

title: Reverse The Chain
description:
A singly linked list stores a sequence of values. Reverse the list so that the last node becomes the first, and print the new order.

Input format:
Line 1: integer n, the number of nodes.
Line 2: n values in list order.

Output format:
The n values in reversed order, separated by single spaces.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 100000.

visibleTestCases.explanation: Read from the other end, the list is 5 4 3 2 1.
The two nodes swap places.

title: Longest Rising Run
description:
Given a list of integers, find the length of the longest strictly increasing subsequence. A subsequence keeps the original order but may skip elements.

Input format:
Line 1: integer n.
Line 2: n integers.

Output format:
One integer, the length of the longest strictly increasing subsequence.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 100000.

visibleTestCases.explanation: One longest choice is 2, 3, 7, 101, so the answer is 4.
Equal values do not count as increasing, so the answer is 1.

title: Count The Clusters
description:
An undirected graph has n nodes labelled 0 to n-1 and m edges. Two nodes belong to the same cluster if you can walk from one to the other along edges. Count the clusters.

Input format:
Line 1: two integers n and m.
Next m lines: two integers u and v, meaning there is an edge between u and v.

Output format:
One integer, the number of clusters.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 100000, 0 <= m <= 200000.

visibleTestCases.explanation: Nodes {0,1,2} form one cluster and {3,4} form another, so the answer is 2.
There are no edges, so every node is its own cluster and the answer is 4.

title: Merge Two Sorted Chains
description:
Two linked lists are each sorted in non-decreasing order. Merge them into one sorted list and print it.

Input format:
Line 1: integer n, the length of the first list.
Line 2: n integers.
Line 3: integer m, the length of the second list.
Line 4: m integers.

Output format:
All n + m values in non-decreasing order, separated by single spaces.

Constraints:
1 <= n, m <= 50000.

visibleTestCases.explanation: Interleaving the two lists in order gives 1 1 2 3 4 4.
Every value in the second list is smaller, so it goes first.

title: Fewest Edits
description:
Given two lowercase words, find the minimum number of single-letter edits needed to turn the first word into the second. An edit is one of: insert a letter, delete a letter, or replace a letter.

Input format:
Line 1: the first word.
Line 2: the second word.

Output format:
One integer, the minimum number of edits.

Constraints:
1 <= length of each word <= 500.

visibleTestCases.explanation: Replace h with r, remove r, remove e: three edits.
Replace k with s, replace e with i, insert g: three edits.
